name: Family Reunification (Reagrupamento Familiar)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires the sponsor to have held a valid Portuguese residence permit for at least 2 years.
requirements.fix_path: Wait until the sponsor reaches 2 years of residence.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a valid marriage or registered partnership recognised under Portuguese law (no minor, forced, or polygamous marriages).
This requires the sponsor to show sufficient income and adequate housing.
Nationals of non-Portuguese-speaking countries must complete Portuguese-language and civic/constitutional-values integration measures — CPLP nationals, including Brazilians, are exempt from this.

requirement_groups.name: Spouse/partner — reduced 15-month wait with prior union proof

requirements.blocker_text: This requires the sponsor to have held a valid Portuguese residence permit for at least 15 months, PLUS proof of at least 18 months of prior stable union with the applicant before the sponsor's arrival in Portugal.

requirement_groups.name: Minor or dependent incapacitated children — no waiting period

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being the minor child, or dependent incapacitated child, of a Portuguese resident — no minimum sponsor residence period applies.

evidence_required.document: Marriage/partnership certificate or evidence of prior stable union

sources.title: Diário da República — Lei n.º 61/2025 (Lei de Estrangeiros), Art. 98 family reunification provisions

notes: MAJOR LIVE POLICY EVENT already in force, not pending: Lei n.º 61/2025 (in force 23 October 2025) materially tightened family reunification — the prior regime allowed reunification essentially upon establishing residence; the new law imposes a 2-year wait for spouses/partners (with a 15-month reduced-wait exception given sufficient prior-union proof), while minor/dependent children remain exempt from any waiting period. The decision window itself was also extended from 3 to 9 months — a genuine processing-time change worth surfacing distinctly from the eligibility waiting period, since they're two different clocks that could easily be conflated. A transitional 180-day window (until approximately April 2026) allowed family members already legally in Portugal to regularise under different terms — not encoded as a separate group here since that window has now closed. CPLP exemption from the language/integration-measures requirement is consistent with the broader CPLP preferential pattern seen across pt_student and pt_cplp. citizenship_after_months (84) uses the CPLP/EU 7-year figure as the more favorable case, same convention as other Portugal routes in this dataset — non-CPLP/EU sponsors' family members would use the 10-year (120-month) figure instead.
